grammar_concept.title: The More..., The More...
grammar_concept.rule: Use 'The + comparative, the + comparative' to say that two things change together — as one increases or decreases, so does the other.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: Both halves of the sentence need their own 'the' before the comparative — even though it can feel repetitive, dropping the second 'the' is not correct English.
grammar_concept.example: The more you practise, the more confident you become. The less you sleep, the harder it is to concentrate.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Quanto mais praticas, mais confiante te tornas. Quanto menos dormes, mais difícil é concentrar-te.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: O português usa uma estrutura semelhante ("quanto mais... mais"), mas os alunos tentam frequentemente traduzir palavra a palavra sem repetir "the" na segunda parte quando ela tem sujeito e verbo completos ("The more you practise, more confident you become" — falta o segundo "the"), ou esquecem de usar a forma comparativa em ambas as partes da frase.
grammar_concept.correction: As duas partes da frase precisam sempre de "the" antes do comparativo: "The more..., the more..." — nunca omitir o segundo "the", mesmo que pareça repetitivo em relação ao português.
grammar_concept.real_world_example: Giving advice: "The earlier you start, the easier it will be."

vocabulary.definition_en: feeling sure about your own abilities or about a situation
example_sentences: The more you practise, the more confident you become.

vocabulary.definition_en: to give all your attention to one thing
example_sentences: It's hard to concentrate when you're tired.

vocabulary.definition_en: slowly, over a period of time, rather than suddenly
example_sentences: Her English improved gradually over the year.

exercises.prompt: Complete: The more you practise, ___ you become.
exercises.explanation: A segunda parte também precisa de "the" antes do comparativo: "the more confident".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Omitir o segundo "the" ("more confident you become") é o erro mais comum nesta estrutura.

exercises.prompt: Complete: The less you sleep, ___ it is to concentrate.
exercises.explanation: "Hard" tem uma forma comparativa irregular curta ("harder"), não "more hard" — e precisa do "the" antes.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "more hard" em vez de "harder" é um erro comum, mesmo entre alunos que já sabem a regra do "the...the".

correct_answer: slowly, over a period of time, rather than suddenly
exercises.explanation: "Gradually" descreve uma mudança lenta e progressiva, não repentina.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What does the speaker say happens the earlier you start?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "The earlier you start, the easier it will be."
exercises.transcript: When it comes to learning a language, the earlier you start, the easier it will be — but it's never too late to begin.

exercises.prompt: Read: "The higher you climb, the colder and windier it gets." What happens as you climb higher?
exercises.explanation: O texto diz diretamente que fica "colder and windier" à medida que se sobe mais alto.

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Quanto mais cedo começares, mais fácil será."
correct_answer: The earlier you start, the easier it will be.
exercises.explanation: As duas partes precisam de "the" antes do comparativo: "The earlier..., the easier...".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Omitir o segundo "the" ("The earlier you start, easier it will be") é o erro mais comum aqui.

steps.content: Both halves of "the more..., the more..." usually share a similar rising-then-falling melody, almost like a matched pair — native speakers often speed up slightly through the whole structure, treating it as one fluent unit rather than two separate clauses.

steps.prompt: Say 2-3 sentences about your own life using 'the more/less..., the more/less...' — about practice, sleep, work, or any habit.
Write 3 sentences using comparative correlatives ('the more/less..., the more/less...'), each about a different topic.
